html:
The Northern Pomo are the northern branch of the Pomo peoples of California, living in the valleys of Mendocino County, around today's Ukiah and Willits, and out to the coast. Their language, Northern Pomo, is one of seven related Pomoan languages; its last native speakers died in the late 1900s. Their southern neighbours were the Central Pomo.

The Pomo lived in villages along the Russian River and the coast, eating acorns, fish and game. They are famous for their baskets, some woven so finely they could hold water, others decorated with feathers and shell beads. The Russian post at Fort Ross was built in 1812 on the land of the Southern Pomo kin to the south.

The Gold Rush brought settlers who seized Pomo land and forced many Pomo into labour. In 1850 US soldiers killed many Pomo at Clear Lake in the Bloody Island Massacre. Many Northern Pomo now live on small rancherias in Mendocino County.
